scope: One three-image prompt, output 832×480, 124 frames at 24 FPS, seeds 0/1/2; 9 clips. This is a pilot, not a broad quality-equivalence study.
fixed: 1× PRO 5000, QAD checkpoint, CAKE attention, 36L decoder, DiT+encoder layerwise offload, same source files/prompt/seeds.
clip_descriptions: A young man with dark curly hair, a white T-shirt and silver wraparound sunglasses joins a family dinner in a warmly lit traditional Japanese room.
A young man wearing silver wraparound sunglasses with dark lenses.
reference_matching: Person and glasses: mean over sampled frames of the maximum cosine across a full frame plus nine fixed half-width/half-height windows. Scene: full-reference to full-frame cosine. Identical evaluator preprocessing for every policy; original references are always the evaluator inputs.
temporal: DINO adjacency is measured on the sampled frames. Optical flow and warp residual use all 123 adjacent frame pairs, downsampled to 208×120. Camera/object movement and occlusions affect these descriptive measures.
uncertainty: Paired differences aggregate each entire clip first. Two-sided 95% Student-t intervals use three seed-pair differences (df=2); frames are not independent samples. Intervals describe seed variation for this one prompt only.
adoption_rule: Prefer match only for a validated workload when reference detail, prompt/action completion, temporal quality and audio show no material regression. These uncalibrated proxies alone cannot pass that gate. No universal numeric margin or official VBench score is asserted.
limitations: DINO/CLIP are appearance/semantic proxies, not calibrated face-identity or small-detail recognizers.
Static frames do not verify action ordering, speech or lip synchronization.
Stability can reward static videos; always inspect motion and the original MP4.
Three seeds for one prompt cannot establish general non-inferiority.
